thread:
sam: Noticed a 6% blip in unassigned leads during an 8-minute window last night. Pattern looks different from previous 'nightshift' spikes. Anyone see anything odd on enrichment or webhook side? :thinking:
irene: Logs show a short-lived vendor latency burst but more interestingly our routing TTL was at 25s and a bunch of leads hit 24-26s. Looks like a tight margin issue rather than wholesale failure.
diego: margin issue makes sense. Proposal: run a routing-time-budget probe A/B where 10% of inbound get TTL=40s and 90% keep 25s for 24h. Measure assign_delta and overflow rate. Low-risk and data-driven.
salesops-bot: FYI sales reported 7 tickets about "missing leads" overnight; all were in unassigned and tied to that 8-minute window.
irene: agree with A/B. We should also add a HubSpot workflow to tag `ttl_probe_group` so we can filter and backfill only affected group if needed. Small HS rule: set `ttl_probe_group` = experiment_a for 10% where `random <= 0.1`.
diego: I'll wire the experiment and the telemetry: metric `assign_success_rate_by_ttl` and `assign_latency_percentile`. Also create a dashboard tile for quick ops checks. Command I'll run: `infractl experiment create ttl_probe --pct 10 --ttl 40s --metrics assign_success_rate_by_ttl`.
sam: timeline? We need to notify Sales before experiments so they don't panic.
irene: I'll draft a short heads-up for Sales: "We're running a short routing-time probe to validate TTL margin — small percentage of inbound may have slightly delayed assignment; we'll reprocess if anything shows unassigned after 2h."
diego: experiment scheduled now. Canaries to 1% first. I'll post canary results in 20m.
enrich-bot: Enrichment vendor latency spike detected at 2025-02-12T03:11Z (p95=62s) for 4m window. Retries observed.
diego: canary results after 20m: no visible increase in duplicates, assign_success_rate improved for TTL=40s group by +2.8% during the window. Overflow rate unchanged.
sam: good signal. Do we keep 40s for all night windows or move to a dynamic TTL?
irene: prefer dynamic TTL tied to live vendor p95. Short-term we can set a rule: if vendor_p95_last_5m > 30s then set routing_ttl=45s for a short window. Longer-term: implement `assignable_time_budget` that incorporates webhook retries, enrich p95, and RR claim latency.
diego: I'll implement the dynamic toggle as a follow-up ticket and schedule it for sprint next week. For now, rollout 40s for night windows and keep the experiment running for another 24h to collect weekday data.
sam: sales note ready. I'll ping the sales channel and pin the message. Also add a runbook step: if assign_delta > 3% trigger immediate TTL bump and start backfill.
salesops-bot: Sales notified. Message: "Quick note — Ops running a short routing-time experiment to reduce missed assignments during transient enrichment slowness. Expect a small reduction in immediate assignment speed for a tiny subset; ops will backfill any unassigned leads."
irene: thanks. Creating postmortem stub and ticket list: dynamic-ttl, assignable_time_budget-metric, hs-ttl-probe-tagging. Will share links once created.
diego: keeping experiment id ttl_probe_2025_02_12 running. Posting daily summary in this thread.
sam: closing loop for now. Nice, data-driven fix rather than an SOS toggle. :thumbsup:
